Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Kahf (The Cave), because it contains the divine miracle in the story of the People of the Cave, which the surah recounts in detail. It is a proof of God's extraordinary power to revive the dead and resurrect them. The word al-Kahf does not occur in any other surah.

Among the Surah's Objectives

• To highlight the sending down of the Qur'an upon the Prophet (ﷺ), that it is a revelation from God Most High, that the Resurrection is true, and to affirm the Oneness of God and deny that He has a son, which is what the people of polytheism ascribed to Him.

• The mention of a number of stories, such as the account of the People of the Cave, the story of the owner of the two gardens, the story of Adam with Iblis, the story of Musa (Moses) with al-Khidr (peace be upon them), and the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, along with the lessons contained therein. The most important of these is the affirmation of God's power to give life after death, to resurrect, and to hold reckoning, and that He, glorified and exalted is He, is able to act contrary to the customary laws (sunan) that people are accustomed to, and that the believer is rewarded with a good recompense, and that the disbeliever meets the consequence of his disbelief in this world or in the Hereafter.

• The establishment of fundamental principles in people's lives through the three most prominent stories: sacrifice for the sake of religion, represented in the story of the People of the Cave; humility in seeking knowledge, represented in the story of Musa with al-Khidr (peace be upon them); and coming to the aid of the oppressed and the weak by a person of authority, represented in the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn.

• Guidance and reinforcement of the Prophet (ﷺ), clarifying that the truth lies in what he reported, that his companions who stayed close to him are better than the chiefs of the polytheists, the depiction of the believer and the disbeliever, the reminder of the consequences for nations that denied the messengers, the nullification of polytheism and the warning to its adherents, and the promise to the believers of the opposite of them.

• Addressing some false notions, such as clarifying that truth is not tied to abundance of wealth, status, and authority, nor to a person's loftiness, but is rather tied to the creed to which the Qur'an calls. This meaning is embodied in the story of the owner of the two gardens.

[Tafsir]

Praise of God through His attributes, all of which are attributes of perfection, and through His apparent and hidden blessings, both religious and worldly, who graciously sent down the Qur'an upon His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and did not place in it any deviation from the truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 9:

Do not think, O Messenger, that the story of the People of the Cave and the inscribed tablet bearing their names is among Our signs that is strange and wondrous; for the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them is more wondrous than that.

Recall, O Messenger, when the young men of faith took refuge in the cave, fearing the trial their people would inflict upon them and their compulsion to worship idols. They said: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself, that will make us steadfast and protect us from evil, and make easy for us the right path that leads us to the deeds You love, so that we may be rightly guided and not go astray."
So We cast deep sleep upon them, and they remained in the cave for many years.

Then We woke them from their sleep, so that We might make manifest to the people what We had known from eternity, that it might become clear which of the two disputing groups was more precise in reckoning the length of their stay: did they remain a day or part of a day, or a long period?

We relate to you, O Messenger, their story in truth. Indeed, the People of the Cave were youths who believed in their Lord and obeyed His command, and We increased them in guidance and steadfastness upon the truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 16:

And when you separated yourselves from your people and their religion, and abandoned what they worship of deities, except the worship of Allah, then take refuge in the cave in the mountain to worship your Lord alone. Then, when they had done that, God cast sleep over them and preserved them. So the heat of the sun does not harm them, and the air does not cut off from them. That which We did with these youths is among the signs of God's power. Whomever God grants success to be guided by His signs, he is the one granted success to the truth; and whomever God does not grant success to, you will not find for him any helper to guide him to the truth, because granting success and forsaking are in the hand of God alone.

And you would think them awake, while they are in fact asleep. We turn them over from side to side, so that the earth does not consume them. This is the commentary of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the Muyassar tafsir, produced by the King Fahd Complex) on Surah al-Kahf, verse 20:

If your people discover you, they will stone you to death or force you back into their religion, and then you will become disbelievers, and you will never attain your goal of entering Paradise, should you do that, ever.

So God made their discovery of the People of the Cave a proof for the believers against the disbelievers. After their affair became clear and they had died, a group of those who came upon them said: "Build a structure over the entrance of the cave that will conceal them, and leave them to themselves; their Lord knows best their condition." And those who held authority and influence over them said: "We will surely take a place of worship (masjid) over their site." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade taking the graves of the prophets and righteous people as places of worship (masajid), and he cursed those who did so in his final injunctions to his community. Likewise, he forbade building over graves in general, plastering them, and writing upon them, because that is from excessive devotion (ghuluww), which may lead to the worship of those buried in them.

In such hardships, protection and victory belong to God, the Truth. He is the best in reward and the best in outcome for those among His believing servants who turn to Him.

Strike for them, O Messenger, a parable of the life of this world, especially for those among them who are full of arrogance: its splendor and how quickly it passes away. And Allah is ever Capable of everything, meaning: He possesses great power over everything.

Wealth and children are adornment and strength in this transient world. The Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 18, verse 80:

"As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers. We feared that he would burden them with rebellion and disbelief, out of their love for him or their need for him, if he had lived."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 81:

So We intended that Allah replace them with one better than him in righteousness, in religion, and in dutifulness toward them.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 82:

As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, and beneath it lay a treasure belonging to them, of gold and silver. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord willed that they should reach maturity and attain their full strength, and then extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord toward them. I did not do what I did, O Musa, on my own accord: everything you saw me do was done by command, not by my own judgment. That which I have explained to you is the meaning of the matters over which you could not restrain yourself from asking and objecting to me.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 83:

"O Messenger, these polytheists among your people ask you about the account of Dhu al-Qarnayn, the righteous king. Say to them: I will recount to you a report of him that you will remember and take as a lesson."

We have established him firmly in the land, and We gave him from every thing a means and a way, by which he could reach whatever he wished, such as conquering cities, subduing enemies, and other things.
So he followed those means and paths with earnestness and diligence.

Until, when he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting into a spring of murky, black mud, and he found near it a people. We said: "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish them, by killing or otherwise, if they do not acknowledge the Oneness of God, or you treat them kindly and teach them guidance and show them the right way."

Dhul-Qarnayn said: "As for him who wrongs himself among them and disbelieves in his Lord, we will punish him in this world. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a great punishment in the Fire of Hell."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 88:

As for whoever among them believes in his Lord, affirms Him, declares His oneness, and acts in obedience to Him, then for him is the Garden as a reward from Allah, and We will show him kindness, and speak gently to him, and make his dealings easy.
Then Dhul-Qarnayn turned back toward the east, following the means that Allah had given him.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 18, verse 90:

Until, when he reached the place where the sun rises, he found it rising upon a people who had no buildings to shelter them, and no trees to shade them from the sun.
Thus it was: Our knowledge encompassed what he had of good and of great means, wherever he turned and traveled.
Then Dhu al-Qarnayn set out, following the routes and means that We had granted him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 93:

Until, when he reached the gap between the two mountains, he found below them a people who could scarcely understand any speech.

O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj, who are two great peoples from the descendants of Adam, are causing corruption in the earth by destroying the crops and the offspring. So, shall we give you a payment and gather wealth for you, on condition that you place between us and them a barrier that will prevent them from reaching us?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, a simplified tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis)) on surah 18, verse 95:

Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "What my Lord has given me of kingship and authority is better than your wealth. So help me with strength from you, and I will set up a barrier between you and them."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 96:

"Bring me blocks of iron, until, when he had leveled [the gap] between the two mountain sides, he said to the workers, 'Blow [the bellows] until, when it had become all fire, he said, "Bring me molten copper to pour over it."'"
So Gog and Magog were unable to climb over the barrier, because of its height and smoothness, and they were unable to dig through it from its base, because of its great width and strength.

Dhul-Qarnayn said: "This wall that I have built, as a barrier against the corruption of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, is a mercy from my Lord toward the people. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will level it to the ground, flattened and crushed, and the promise of my Lord is always true."

And We shall leave them, Gog and Magog, on that Day when Our promise comes to them, surging against one another in confusion because of their multitude. And the Trumpet will be blown for the Resurrection, and We shall gather all of creation together for reckoning and recompense.
And We will present Hell to the disbelievers on that Day, displaying it before them so that We may show them the evil consequence of their disbelief.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 101:**

Those whose eyes were, in the world, under a covering from My remembrance, so they could not see My signs, and they could not bear to hear My proofs that lead to belief in Me and in My Messenger.
﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as allies instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.﴾
Say, O Messenger, to the people as a warner: Shall we inform you of those who are the greatest losers in their deeds?

This is the commentary on Qur'an 18:104 (Surah al-Kahf) from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

"They are those whose effort was lost in the life of this world, and they are the polytheists of your people and others who strayed from the right way, so they were not upon guidance or correctness, while they thought that they were doing good in their deeds."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 18, verse 105:

Those are the ones who have lost the most in their deeds: they are the ones who denied the signs of their Lord and rejected them, and who denied meeting Him on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore their deeds came to nothing because of their disbelief, and on the Day of Resurrection We will assign them no weight.

That is their recompense, the prepared punishment for the nullifying of their deeds: it is the Fire of Hell, because of their disbelief in Allah and their taking His signs and the proofs of His messengers in mockery and ridicule.
Indeed, those who believed in Me, affirmed My messengers, and did righteous deeds, will have the highest abodes of Paradise and its middle abodes, and it is the best of them in station.
"Abiding therein forever, they will not desire any removal from it, for their longing for it and their love of it."

Say, [O Messenger]: Even if the sea were ink for the pens with which the words of Allah are written, [words] of His knowledge and His wisdom, and what He revealed to His angels and messengers, the sea would be exhausted before the words of Allah were exhausted. And even if We brought the like of it as additional supply, [another seas] to it. In the verse is an affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, the Exalted, in reality, as befits His majesty and perfection.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds that conform to His law, and let him not associate anyone with his Lord in worship."
